_coords: tapFrac is computed from each control's real RectTransform, NOT estimated. The canvas is Expand @1242x2688, so on the 1080x2400 capture device it resolves to 1242x2760 logical, and an AspectRatioFitter (FitInParent, 1242/2688) letterboxes the panel by 36 logical units top and bottom. Hence: fracX = (621 + x_from_panel_centre) / 1242 and fracY = (36 + y_from_panel_top) / 2760. Using 2688 as the denominator, or dropping the 36, shifts every tap 16-26 device px down - small enough that it still lands and large enough to eat the margin on a 92-unit control.
_timing: Watch clock t=0 at WatchDirector.Start (the game scene's own loader is 0.4 s, which waitLoader absorbs). With no input at all the harbourmaster assist resolves a step every 5.0 s, dropping to 3.5 s once two flags are down, so the baseline is flag 1 at 15 s, flag 2 at 30 s, flag 3 at 40.5 s. The one board tap of step 6 resets the idle timer, which pushes the whole chain later: the EARLIEST the HARBOUR LOG can fire is ~45 s (9 steps: the tap plus assists at 14.2 / 19.2 / 24.2 / 29.2 / 34.2 / 37.7 / 41.2 / 44.7). Step 5 is captured at ~9 s (board up, one pip), step 6 at ~27 s (a flag planted, the board visibly changed), step 7 opens the pause card at ~30 s - a 15 s margin before the log can possibly exist, so PAUSE can never land on the log instead - and step 8 resumes and waits 38 s, landing at ~66 s with the log up and ~20 s of margin. Pausing freezes the drain and the activity timers, so the two seconds spent on the pause card do not count against any of this.
